content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper considers the named entity recognition (NER) problem when entities are not fully annotated. This can be viewed as a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning problem and the difficult part is to distinguish unlabeled entities from negative instances. Starting from experimental results, the authors propose a new PU-learning algorithm which distinguishes unlabeled entities from negative instances. The presented experimental results on benchmark Chinese NER datasets are promising.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros
* address of an interesting PU-learning problem
* experimental results are very promising

Cons
* Selection process based on the early stage of learning in a NN
* Selection of hyperparameters and their influence should be detailed
* Seems to be incremental work
* Should be submitted in an NLP conference
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The description of the problem is rather clear as well as the ideas behind the proposed method. Sections 3.2 and 3.3 should be made clearer. The main contribution is a new way to distinguish unlabeled entities from negative instances in a preprocessing step but the work is mainly incremental. The problem is significant but, in my opinion, mainly for the NLP community. I am doubtful about reproducibility.

Detailed comments.
* Construction of \hat{D} could be made more clear. You introduce a non-entity label whic is moved in BMES tag or BI tag (which one?) while before you were considering the BIO tagging. This depends on the original system? 
* And \hat{D} will be the input of the original system?
* It should be made clear that the angle-based technique is a try to improve the Detect module
* Implement of CRF. This has not be discussed before. What is the CRF for? In whic system? 
* You should give a precise description of how are chosen hyperparameters values because annotated entities are scarce. You should give the hyperpameter values chosen for every experiment. Also a study on the dependency of the experimental results wrt the hyperparameter values should be given.
* It is not clear to me why the method works better for BERT and LEBERT on synthetic datasets.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper considers the named entity recognition (NER) problem when entities are not fully annotated. The authors propose to distinguish unlabeled entities from negative instances using a selection process based on the early stage of learning in a NN. If the experimental results seem very promising, I think that the paper is not ready for publication at ICLR. Also I think that an NLP conference should be a better choice to submit a revised version.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to mitigate the misguidance of unlabeled entities for NER through a two-step method. The first step is a PU learning algorithm, which distinguishes some unlabelled entities from negative instances based on a confidence threshold with an angle-based classifier. The second step is a random sampling process on the remaining characters with an O tag. The authors verify the effectiveness of the proposed method on many NER models and datasets consisting of synthesized and real-world ones.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths**

- The motivation is clearly described and illustrated by statistical figures: representation of unlabeled entities and characters with true O (in BIO or BMESO) tag diversified at the early training step, and only a small proportion of O-chars with low confidence tend to be true unlabeled entities.

- The proposed pipeline and angle-based techniques are reasonable, delivering significant performance improvement on synthesized datasets.

**Weaknesses**

- The novelty is somewhat limited for two reasons. Firstly, a two-step pipeline is a common technical design for PU learning. The difference here, to my knowledge,  is that previous works focus on finding high-confidence negatives, while this work identifies some false negatives (unlabeled entities). Secondly, the negative sampling process in NER has been widely studied.

- The empirical results are not convincing enough, and the experiment design can be strengthened. 

	-  I  wonder why datasets of only Chinese but no other languages are used. 
	-  There is no investigation into how the two steps collaborate and contribute to the overall performance.
	- Angle-based design is only verified on the Webo dataset. Its effects on other datasets can be easily put into Tables 1-6.
	-  The performance improvements in real-world settings look marginal.

- The overall organization can be improved. 

	-  Though Section 2 clearly depicts the problem and motivation, I feel that it can be merged into Section 1 since the introduction part seemed not to convey much information. 
	-  Figure 1 is not friendly to non-Chinese readers. 
	-  It is kind of weird to put Figure 6 in Section 3.2.
	-  Tables 1 to 4 could be arranged more compactly.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is generally well-written and easy to follow. The technical novelty is limited to my knowledge. There is no released code, though it may not be challenging to reproduce the method. The performance improvements of real-world datasets look marginal, making me wonder whether they are statistically significant or based on a random run.
content.summary_of_the_review: The work is well-motivated, but the proposed two-step pipeline is somewhat incremental, though the angle-based design is impressive (but unfortunately not well justified. The experiments are not convincing, and the analysis is a little weak.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studied the False O-Char problem for unlabeled entities. It discovered that in the early stage of training, the average O-value for unlabeled entities is much smaller than that of the true O-chars. So it detected the False O-Char by the small O-value of a given NER model and generated a new dataset by negative sampling. Then it designed a special learning algorithm to learn from the dataset. The experimental results showed that the proposed algorithm is robust when the proportion of unlabeled entities increases.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weaknesses:

* The paper is built on emperical observations and hyperparameters. No solid theoretical analysis or adaptive learning is involved. 
* The motivation and idea is neither novel nor convincing. 
* The whole procedure is not clearly illustrated. How the NER model should be trained to generate the dataset $\hat{D}$? What the difference between this NER model and the baseline model?
* The performance on real-world dataset is marginal.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
* Clearity: Fair 
* Quality: Fair
* Novelty: Poor
* Reproducibility: Fair
content.summary_of_the_review:
The idea of this paper is not convincing. It lacks deep insight and theoretical analysis. It builds a complex system to modify some labels in the dataset but only gets marginal improvement after searching many hyperparameters. 

I guess the author wants to transfer the False-O problem into a partial label problem, so I would like to suggest that the author read some from the "partial labeled learning" field.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a two-step method to handle the unlabeled entity problem in NER. The proposed method consists of a novel Positive-Unlabeled (PU-learning) algorithm and negative sampling, in which PU-learning distinguishes part of the unlabeled entities from negative instances based on confidence threshold. The paper validates the proposed method in the character-level NER models on several benchmark NER datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
(1) The paper handles a very practical and important real-world problem in NER.
(2) The solution is simple and easy to follow.
(3) The experiments are extensive, including multiple NER models on multiple real-world datasets.

Weakness:
(1) In general, the improvements compared to previous SOTA seem to be limited. Considering the limited improvements, test of significance results may need to be provided.
(2) The paper may also discuss (or evaluate) the potentials of the proposed approach in NER tasks which are not character-level NER. Several compared baselines (e.g., in Table 6) seem to be not originally design for character-level NER. It is unclear whether the comparison is fair for these baselines.
(3) Why the baselines in Table 5 and 6 are chosen to be different? It seems that limited discussions are provided.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper handles a very practical and important real-world problem in NER. In extensive experiments, the proposed method outperforms several baselines, when using multiple NER models on multiple real-world datasets.

The paper in general is easy to follow. Some more discussions in the experiments can be helpful to clarify some questions. (e.g., Why the baselines in Table 5 and 6 are chosen to be different? Test of significance results? Is the comparison setting fair for baselines which are not for character-level NER).

The proposed solution is novel in NER.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper proposes a two-step method to handle the unlabeled entity problem in NER. In general, the improvements compared to previous SOTA seem to be limited. Considering the limited improvements, test of significance results may need to be provided. Some descriptions and settings in experiments are not that clear.

content.title: Paper Decision
content.metareview:_summary,_strengths_and_weakn: The paper studies NER under the case of  partially annotated  data. The reviewers agree  that: 1) it is unclear what new elements are brought to the table in the commonly used two-step method;  2) technical novelty or insight is currently limited in the paper's current form. 3) the improvements are marginal.  The authors are encouraged to continue their work, address reviewer concerns, and  resubmit at a future conference at ICLR or other venues.
